categories.name: File Path Resolution
categories.description: Functions to resolve file paths and access user files

categories.name: Data Access
categories.description: Functions to access geographic data stored in PostGIS database

functions.name: get_assets_path
functions.description: Resolve a relative path within the assets folder. Convenient helper for accessing files in your assets directory.

parameters.name: relative_path
parameters.description: Path relative to assets folder (e.g., 'file.geojson' or 'folder/file.geojson'). Can also include username prefix for convenience.

returns.description: Absolute file path within assets directory

examples.title: Access file in assets root
examples.code:
# Access file directly in assets folder
file_path = get_assets_path('kenya_boundary.geojson')
gdf = gpd.read_file(file_path)
examples.description: Access a file in the root of assets folder

examples.title: Access file in subfolder
examples.code:
# Access file in subfolder
file_path = get_assets_path('data/kenya_boundary.geojson')
gdf = gpd.read_file(file_path)
examples.description: Access a file in a subfolder within assets

examples.title: With full path
examples.code:
# Also works with full path including username
file_path = get_assets_path('username_earthcode/assets/file.geojson')
# Automatically extracts the assets part
examples.description: The function extracts the assets part from full paths

functions.name: get_area_by_name
functions.description: Retrieve an Area object from PostGIS database by name. Returns an Area object with geometry attribute that can be used with geopandas.

returns.description: Area object with 'geom' attribute containing the geometry (MultiPolygon)

examples.title: Basic usage
examples.code:
# Get area by name
import geopandas as gpd

area = get_area_by_name('Kenya_boundary')
# Convert to GeoDataFrame
gdf = gpd.GeoDataFrame([{'geometry': area.geom}], crs='EPSG:4326')
print(gdf)
examples.description: Retrieve an area and convert to GeoDataFrame

examples.title: Use in analysis
examples.code:
# Get area and use for spatial operations
area = get_area_by_name('Kenya_boundary')
gdf = gpd.GeoDataFrame([{'name': 'Kenya', 'geometry': area.geom}], crs='EPSG:4326')

# Calculate area
area_km2 = gdf.geometry.area.sum() / 1e6
print(f"Area: {area_km2:.2f} km²")
examples.description: Use the area for spatial analysis

examples.title: Case-insensitive search
examples.code:
# Name matching is case-insensitive
area1 = get_area_by_name('kenya_boundary')
area2 = get_area_by_name('KENYA_BOUNDARY')
# Both return the same area

notes: Raises ValueError if area not found
Only returns areas belonging to the current user

functions.name: get_area_by_id
functions.description: Retrieve an Area object from PostGIS database by ID. Useful when you know the specific area ID from metadata.

returns.description: Area object with 'geom' attribute containing the geometry (MultiPolygon)

examples.title: Basic usage
examples.code:
# Get area by ID
import geopandas as gpd

area = get_area_by_id(1)
# Convert to GeoDataFrame
gdf = gpd.GeoDataFrame([{'geometry': area.geom}], crs='EPSG:4326')
print(gdf)
examples.description: Retrieve an area by its ID

examples.title: Using area ID from metadata
examples.code:
# When you know the area ID from file metadata
area_id = 5  # From file.metadata.postgis_area_id
area = get_area_by_id(area_id)
gdf = gpd.GeoDataFrame([{'geometry': area.geom}], crs='EPSG:4326')
examples.description: Use area ID from file metadata

examples.title: Error handling
examples.description: Handle errors when area is not found

notes: Raises ValueError if area not found or doesn't belong to user
Useful when you have the area ID from metadata
